recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Recreate **Neo-Tokyo Overtime: Zombie Shooter** as a portrait-first browser canvas game. Preserve the source mechanics exactly: a survival shooter with tap/click point shooting, projected zombies approaching from z-depth, one defeated enemy per successful shot, score +1 per defeated threat, health starting at 100, -20 health per close contact, RUN/shake retreat that pushes enemies back by reducing approach speed, score-scaled spawn pressure, game-over at zero health, and retry reset.

Transform the presentation into a satirical futuristic after-work zombie shooter. The player is a Chad Courier with a neon capsule hand-cannon on a Neo-Tokyo expressway. Enemies are infected salary-zombie commuters. Use neon noir cyan/pink/gold/lime, shonen speed-lines, manga impact flashes, compact leaderboard HUD language, and meme feedback such as “CHAD SHOT” and “POGGERS STREAK.” Keep all UI readable and tappable in 4:7 to 9:16 portrait mobile ranges.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source Truth
- genre: first-person / camera-facing arcade zombie shooter survival
- objective: survive as long as possible by tapping/clicking approaching threats before they reach close range
- input model: tap/click canvas to shoot; hold RUN button or shake device to create retreat energy
- core loop: spawn distant zombie -> zombie approaches in z-depth -> player shoots one target with point hit detection or retreats -> score increases on hit -> health drops when a zombie reaches the player -> repeat until health reaches zero
- fail/friction state: five close contacts at 20 damage each deplete 100 health and open a game-over/retry screen

## Protected Mechanics
- point-and-shoot canvas input, one shot per tap/click, and one defeated target per shot
- perspective z-depth enemy approach, score-based spawn interval reduction, RUN/shake retreat subtracting from approach speed
- score +1 per defeated zombie, health starts at 100, close contact costs 20 health, game over at health <= 0, restart resets state

## Safe Theming Surfaces
HUD copy, title, buttons, enemy silhouette art, gun art, background, particles, fonts, colors, reaction text, audio helper wiring, and progression labels are presentation-only and safe to transform.
